requestedActions.title: List repository names visible to the connected person, with pagination

guide.summary: Forgejo documents an OAuth2 provider with the Authorization Code Grant, PKCE and public or confidential clients. Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens, so an OAuth token acts with the user's full rights and no grant identifier is applicable. The app must restrict itself to read-only GET calls. Repository listing uses documented GET endpoints with page-based pagination. Instances where the user is an administrator can be affected by administrative token rights. Customer-admin, provider review and marketplace policies are not in the supplied sources.
guide.recommendation: Forgejo documents an OAuth2 provider with the Authorization Code Grant, PKCE and public or confidential clients. findings.title: OAuth2 tokens have no scope boundary on Forgejo
findings.detail: Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can execute any action on behalf of the user, not just Git actions. Read-only behavior must be enforced by the app, not by the token.
findings.appliesWhen: Using the OAuth2 provider for this read-only repository listing.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.

findings.title: Third-party OAuth applications receive administrative rights
findings.detail: A third-party application obtaining a token for a user through an OAuth2 application will have administrative rights. This applies even though the app only reads repository names.
findings.appliesWhen: The connected person is or may be a Forgejo instance administrator, or the token is issued for an instance administrator account.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

findings.title: Register an OAuth2 application on each customer instance
findings.detail: Applications are registered at the user settings applications page for an individual user, or at the admin applications page for instance-wide use. Registration yields client credentials and a redirect URI needed for the Authorization Code flow. Public clients use PKCE and a loopback redirect where applicable.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer instance base URL is supplied and the customer connects their own account.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

findings.title: Use the OAuth2 access token as a bearer credential against the API
findings.detail: Access tokens from the OAuth2 provider are accepted in the Authorization: Bearer header or as token or access_token query parameters. The token is obtained at the access token endpoint after authorization.
findings.appliesWhen: Calling the repository list endpoints after the authorization code exchange.

evidence.quote: Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.
Authorization Endpoint /login/oauth/authorize Access Token Endpoint /login/oauth/access_token

steps.title: Register an OAuth2 application on the customer instance
steps.detail: The customer signs in to their own Forgejo instance and registers an OAuth2 application at user settings applications, obtaining a client ID and secret and a redirect URI. Public clients use PKCE and a loopback redirect where applicable.
steps.doneWhen: The customer has a client ID, a client secret (for confidential clients) and a registered redirect URI for the app.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: the customer's own Forgejo base URL, supplied by the customer
CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET: returned when the application is registered

steps.title: Redirect the connected person to the authorization endpoint and check the callback
steps.detail: Send the user to the documented authorization endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and a state value. The user consents in their browser; the app verifies the returned state and code on the callback. Scopes are not implemented, so the consent covers the user's full rights.
steps.doneWhen: The callback returns a code and the matching state value.

evidence.quote: https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an application in the settings. The STATE is a random string that will be
The user will now be asked to authorize your application. If they authorize it, the user will be redirected to the REDIRECT_URL , for example:
sent back to your application after the user authorizes. The state parameter is optional but should be used to prevent CSRF attacks.

fields: client_id: from the registered application
redirect_uri: must match the registered redirect URI exactly
state: random string generated by the app and checked on callback
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: POST the returned code to the documented access token endpoint with grant_type authorization_code. Confidential clients send client_secret; public PKCE clients send code_verifier instead. The redirect_uri must match the authorization request. Use the returned access_token for read calls.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains access_token and token_type bearer.

The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

steps.doneWhen: The response returns a 200 with a data array of repository objects and an x-total-count header. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register an OAuth2 application on the customer instance
The customer signs in to their own Forgejo instance and registers an OAuth2 application at user settings applications, obtaining a client ID and secret and a redirect URI. Public clients use PKCE and a loopback redirect where applicable.
Fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: the customer's own Forgejo base URL, supplied by the customer, CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET: returned when the application is registered

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Redirect the connected person to the authorization endpoint and check the callback
Done when: The callback returns a code and the matching state value.

Exchange the authorization code for an access token
Done when: The token response contains access_token and token_type bearer.

Read the first page of visible repositories
Done when: The response returns a 200 with a data array of repository objects and an x-total-count header. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

Follow pagination until the documented end condition
Done when: The app has collected names until no rel=next link remains and the count matches x-total-count. Page 2 has been read and the Link header is checked for a further rel=next. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
